# Leafony Docs

> Official technical documentation for Leafony, an IoT development platform for prototyping devices by stacking small boards called "leaves". Covers kits, each leaf's specifications, development environments (STM32, AVR, ESP32), sample apps, and troubleshooting. Leafony is made and sold by Mitdir Inc. Most pages are written in Japanese; English translations are under /en/.

Answer from these pages and cite the page URL. When a question depends on a specific leaf, ask for the model printed on the board, including the final letter (for example AZ01C). For questions the documentation does not cover, point to the question form at https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/ask/ ; for orders, shipping, or faults, point to https://shop.leafony.com/pages/contact-us .

The full text of every page is in https://docs.leafony.com/en/llms-full.txt (English) and https://docs.leafony.com/llms-full.txt (Japanese).

## Discover and choose Leafony

- [About Leafony: A Compact, Low-Power IoT Development Platform](https://docs.leafony.com/en/overview/): Build IoT prototypes with small sensor, wireless and display boards. Learn about Leafony, choose a kit, set up development tools and try sample applications.
- [Kits and products](https://docs.leafony.com/en/products/): Explore Leafony kits, individual leaves and accessories, with links to documentation and the shop.
- [Basic Kit 2: Build BLE Sensors with AVR and STM32](https://docs.leafony.com/en/products/basic2/): Explore the leaves and accessories in Leafony Basic Kit 2, measure temperature, humidity, light and acceleration, and try AVR and STM32 BLE sensor demos.
- [Cellular LPWA Cat-M1 Kit](https://docs.leafony.com/en/products/cellular-lpwa-cat-m1/): Explore environmental sensing and cellular communication with the Cellular LPWA Cat-M1 Kit. Check its leaves, accessories, development preparation and documentation.
- [Leafony case studies](https://docs.leafony.com/en/cases/): Explore how Leafony is used in the field, in research and trials, and in creative projects. Case studies are being prepared.

## Get started

- [Run your kit](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/): Find the first steps for your Leafony kit. Try a preinstalled demo or follow the Cat-M1 Kit guide to record sensor data in Google Sheets.
- [Assembling and Replacing Leaves](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/assembly/): Check power before stacking leaves, attach ACR connectors, use spacers, secure the stack with screws and a Nut Plate, and test your new configuration.
- [Basic Kit / Basic Kit 2: Your First AVR Demo](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/basic/): Use the preinstalled AVR demo to view temperature, humidity, illuminance and acceleration over BLE. These first steps are shared by Basic Kit and Basic Kit 2 and need no development tools.
- [Basic Kit 2: Try STM32 Logging and BLE](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/basic2/): An optional guide to sensor logging and BLE after swapping in the STM32 MCU included in Basic Kit 2. Start with the assembled AVR demo when your kit arrives.
- [ESP32 Wi-Fi Kit / Kit 2 Getting Started Guide](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/esp32/): Try the Wi-Fi-equipped Leaf!
- [STM32 MCU Getting Started Guide](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/stm32/): Choose a development tool for STM32 MCU, review the preparation overview, and find setup guides and your first examples.
- [Cat-M1 Kit Start Guide](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/cellular-lpwa-cat-m1/): Send temperature and humidity directly to the cloud with the compact, low-power Cellular LPWA Cat-M1 Kit. Check the contents, assemble the kit, upload the sample, and record data in Google Sheets.

## Write programs

- [Environment Setting](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/): Find the development environment setup guide for your Leafony STM32, AVR, or ESP32 processor leaf.
- [Libraries and board definitions](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/libraries/): Choose board definitions for your Leafony MCU and find the libraries and installation methods used by the examples.
- [STM32 MCU Development Environment Settings Manual](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/stm32/)
- [STM32 MCU: Arduino IDE Setup](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/stm32/arduino_ide/): Set up Arduino IDE for the AP03 STM32 MCU leaf and upload a program.
- [STM32 MCU: PlatformIO Setup](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/stm32/platformio/): Set up PlatformIO for the AP03 STM32 MCU leaf and upload a program.
- [How to connect the debugger](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/stm32/stm32_debug/)
- [STM32 MCU: STM32CubeIDE Setup](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/stm32/stm32cube_ide/): Build an AP03 STM32 Hello World project, upload it over UART and check serial output.
- [AVR MCU Development Environment Settings Manual](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/avr/)
- [AVR MCU: Arduino IDE Setup](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/avr/arduino/): Set up Arduino IDE for the AP01 AVR MCU leaf and upload a program.
- [AVR MCU: PlatformIO Setup](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/avr/platformio/): Set up PlatformIO for the AP01 AVR MCU leaf and upload a program.
- [ESP32 MCU Development Environment Settings Manual](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/esp32/): Set up Arduino IDE or PlatformIO for the Leafony AP02 ESP32 MCU leaf. Choose a development tool and follow its installation and program upload guide.
- [ESP32 MCU: Arduino IDE Setup](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/esp32/arduino/): Set up Arduino IDE for the AP02 ESP32 MCU leaf and upload a program.
- [ESP32 MCU: PlatformIO Setup](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/esp32/platformio/): Set up PlatformIO for the AP02 ESP32 MCU leaf and upload a program.
- [Sample Applications](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/): Find Leafony examples for measuring, recording, sending, displaying, and notifications. Browse all STM32, AVR, and ESP32 examples, development tools, and preparation steps.
- [How to run an example](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/reproducing/): Choose the right Leafony hardware, development tool, and source files, then check the build, upload, and execution results in order.

## Combine and design

- [Combining Leaves and Choosing a Power Supply](https://docs.leafony.com/en/guides/combining-leaves/): Check the MCU and software, power supply, GPIO and communication pins, I2C addresses, and component clearance when combining Leafony leaves.
- [Leafony Bus Specifications and Connections](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leafony-bus/): Learn the names of the 29 Leafony Bus contacts, the roles of 3.3V and VBUS, MCU-specific pin functions, and the power, signal, and size requirements to check.
- [I2C Address Map](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/i2c-address-map/): List of I2C device addresses used on each leaf
- [Low-Power IoT Sensor Design and Battery Runtime Calculations](https://docs.leafony.com/en/lowpower/): Estimate power, average current and battery runtime for Leafony IoT sensors, use STM32 sleep modes and learn how to measure energy use on your device.
- [Measure Current and Reduce Power Consumption](https://docs.leafony.com/en/guides/measuring-power/): Define the measurement boundary and power paths, connect an AX05B and current meter, record an active/transmit/sleep cycle, and compare average current.
- [Home-made leaf development](https://docs.leafony.com/en/pcb/): CAD templates, pin assignments, a pin assignment editor, and the I2C address map for designing your own leaf
- [CR-8000 Design Force Template Design Data](https://docs.leafony.com/en/pcb/cr-8000_design_force/)
- [KiCad Template Project](https://docs.leafony.com/en/pcb/kicad/): How to register the template, configure libraries, and start designing a Leafony expansion leaf with KiCad 10.0.x
- [Pin Assignment Editor](https://docs.leafony.com/en/pcb/pinout-editor/): Create Leafony pin assignment diagrams and tables comparing pin usage across leaves, then download them as PNG or SVG images.

## Help and support

- [Help and questions](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/): Search answers about identifying leaves, power, uploads, connections and using Leafony. Open the question form if you cannot find an answer.
- [Terms](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/): Understand terms used in Leafony documentation: BLE, I2C, SPI and UART communication; MCU, MEMS and PWM; leaves, the Leafony bus and related organizations.

## News and site information

- [License](https://docs.leafony.com/en/license/): Learn about Leafony software and board layout licenses, commercial use, selling your own leaves, and the conditions for using the Leafony trademark.
- [Privacy and analytics](https://docs.leafony.com/en/privacy/): How Leafony documentation uses Google Analytics and Microsoft Clarity.

## Questions and answers

- [FAQ](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/)
- [What supply voltage does AC09 need for cellular communication?](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/ac09-voltage/): AC09 uses a 3.3V supply. For battery operation, we recommend AV06 with an external battery such as dry cells. Learn how this differs from the Basic Kit 2 coin-cell supply.
- [Can I connect an external sensor?](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/external-sensors/): Use an expansion leaf or the AI05 I2C header. Check power, signal levels, pin assignments, and I2C addresses.
- [What sensors are available?](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/sensor-options/): Explore temperature, humidity, light, acceleration, and pressure sensing with AI01 and AI05. Distinguish discontinued AI02/AI03 leaves and optional sensors.
- [Where can I buy Leafony?](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/where-to-buy/): Buy kits and leaves from Leafony Shop. Each product page has current prices, stock, and lead times.
- [Are the wireless leaves certified for use in Japan?](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/radio-certification/): Learn how certified module and antenna combinations work and where to check certification markings on the module.
- [How should I match the STM32 Core and RTC library versions?](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/stm32-rtc-core/): STM32RTC and the Arduino Core require compatible versions. Check current requirements when using an older sample too.
- [Can a Windows C# app receive Leafony BLE data?](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/windows-ble/): With a configuration that supports GATT communication, you can build a receiver using Windows BLE APIs. Start by checking UUIDs and the data format.
- [Where can I find the BLE data format and UUIDs?](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/ble-data-format/): Check the sample’s transmitter and receiver code together. 4-Sensors_BLE is an example that sends comma-separated text.
- [Why can I discover a BLE beacon but not connect to it?](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/ble-beacon-connection/): STM32 Simple BLE Beacon is configured for reading Advertising data without a connection. It serves a different purpose from a connected receiver sample.
- [Should I start with Arduino IDE or PlatformIO?](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/development-tools/): Choose an environment supported by your sample. Check the MCU model and sample configuration before choosing the tool.
- [STM32 program does not run after “upload complete”](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/stm32-upload-run/): Check the AP03 Program/Run switch, reset sequence, and upload verification log. The completion message alone can be misleading.
- [“No such file or directory” error when building a sample](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/library-not-found/): Match the missing header to the library specified by the sample. Similar names can refer to different authors and implementations.
- [Does cellular communication with AC09 need a SIM and a service plan?](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/ac09-sim/): AC09 uses a nanoSIM. Check the 1NCE or SORACOM sample settings alongside your kit and network requirements.
- [Can AC09 send measurements to Google Sheets over cellular communication?](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/ac09-google-sheets/): Sample and settings for sending BME280 temperature and humidity to Google Sheets with the Cat-M1 Kit's AP03B + AI05 + AC09 configuration.
- [I2C sensor stops responding after adding a leaf](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/i2c-address-conflict/): Check for duplicate I2C addresses and pull-up requirements. Combinations such as AI05 with AX06 or AC08 with AC09 need address checks.
- [Which programming languages can I use with STM32?](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/stm32-language/): Leafony AP03 development is intended to use C/C++ with Arduino IDE or STM32CubeIDE. Arduino sketches are based on C++.
- [Can I use Python with Leafony?](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/python/): On-leaf development is intended to use C/C++ with Arduino IDE, or STM32CubeIDE for STM32 leaves. Python can receive and analyze data on a PC.

## Sample apps

- [Blink an LED with STM32CubeIDE](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples-stm/blink/): Use an STM32CubeIDE project to turn the AP03 STM32 MCU LED on and off every second. Covers downloading, importing, building, programming, and checking the result.
- [Read battery](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/beginner/avr-mcu/basic/read_battery/): Read the battery voltage using the AD converter on the CR2032 coin cell leaf.
- [Button](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/beginner/esp32-mcu/esp32/button/): Displays the status of the boot mode switch on the ESP32 MCU leaf on the serial monitor.
- [Temperature and humidity sensor](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/beginner/stm32-mcu/basic/temp_humid_sensors/): This sample reads the value of the temperature and humidity sensor on the 4-Sensors Leaf and displays it on a serial monitor.
- [Read temperature, humidity, pressure and acceleration with AI05](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/beginner/stm32-mcu/env-sensors/): Read environmental data and 3-axis acceleration every second with AP03 and AI05 Env Sensors. Find the required leaves, sample upload steps, measured output and an explanation of the readings.
- [Temperature and humidity sensor](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/beginner/avr-mcu/basic/temp_humid_sensors/): This sample reads the value of the temperature and humidity sensor on the 4-Sensors Leaf and displays it on a serial monitor.
- [Read HTS221 Temperature and Humidity with ESP32](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/beginner/esp32-mcu/basic/temp_humid_sensors/): Use Leafony AP02 ESP32 MCU and AI01 4-Sensors to read HTS221 data in Arduino's serial monitor. Covers assembly, sample code and two-point correction.
- [Illum sensor](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/beginner/stm32-mcu/basic/illum_sensor/): This sample reads the value of the illuminance sensor on the 4-Sensors leaf and displays it on the serial monitor.

- [Google Sheets IoT](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/advanced/avr-mcu/basic/google_sheets_iot/): We will create an IoT environment sensor using Leafony Beacon1) and Raspberry Pi, and visualize the sensor data using Google Spreadsheet.
- [LoRa](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/advanced/avr-mcu/lora/lora/): Using LoRa Easy leaf, sensor data (temperature, humidity, illumination, tilt) can be sent to a distant location and output to a PC terminal.
- [Camera](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/advanced/avr-mcu/exten/camera/): An example of using Seeed Studio's Grove series sensors. Let's try to save an image taken by the camera once a minute to a microSD card.
